leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 files name B050 (Mircea Cărtărescu) as the single preferred configuration, with a single-writer citation. The shared merit case is a distinctive voice, large internally patterned architectures, and memory, the body and dream built into a metaphysical project (Blinding/Orbitor, Solenoid, on public knowledge). Several files add that the poetic origin and essays give generic breadth. The files do not share one rationale for the second tier. Their alternatives differ: Olsson B009 and B018; Sward B018 and B009; Mattson B001 and B009; Carlberg B009 and B013; Palm B009 and B039; Sem-Sandberg B009 and B024. B009 (Zurita) is the only alternative named by all six, but no member prefers it as a first choice in round 1, so it is not listed as a leading position. Every file frames its reading as resting on public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification. The citation wordings for B050 are close but not identical (for example whether Romanian-language is named, and metaphysical scope versus historical reach). They all credit the same single laureate, so the differences are in wording only, not in laureate or scope.

areas_of_agreement: All six members explicitly prefer B050 as the single laureate in round 1, with a single-writer citation and no multiwriter configuration.

All six members attribute the case for B050 to the common criteria (voice, formal architecture, imaginative depth, breadth of the oeuvre), and Sem-Sandberg and Sward explicitly state that opening rank agreement is not evidence of merit.
All six members name translation loss as the main limit on their evidence, and several note that it is more severe for poetry (Zurita, Adonis) than for large-scale prose architecture.
All six members give the same main merit reservation about B050: whether the late, very large volumes deepen the project or repeat its motifs. No file claims to have settled this.

Members who discuss Zurita (B009) agree that any citation would have to rest on the written poetic sequences, with the landscape-scale and non-textual interventions treated only as an extension of them.
Members who discuss Yan Lianke (B024) and Adonis (B013) agree that censorship, political positions and symbolism are context and not literary evidence.
Every file reports no apparent conflict from the supplied profile and treats the member's own literary practice as context, not as a preference signal.
scientific_disputes: Whether the late volumes of Cărtărescu deepen the earlier project or repeat and enclose it (raised in all six files): Mattson and Sem-Sandberg lean toward reading recurrence as a personal mythology or as extension, while Carlberg, Palm, Sward and Olsson treat it as an open test of sustained quality. No file offers verified close-reading evidence on either side.

How much weight Zurita's written sequences can bear on their own: Olsson (in the opening) found the voice and formal seriousness strongest; Sward's reservation is tied to historical context and translation exposure; Sem-Sandberg questions whether the cycle deepens or repeats; Mattson, Carlberg and Palm accept the strength of the case but cite translation exposure of sequence and sound.

Whether Marie NDiaye's compact but tightly controlled oeuvre has the breadth and cumulative weight of a whole-authorship prize. Mattson champions the control and range across fiction and drama; Carlberg, Palm, Sem-Sandberg and Sward doubt the breadth, and several note thinner knowledge of the drama.

Whether the later novels of Yan Lianke keep the quality of The Four Books and The Explosion Chronicles across a large and possibly uneven corpus. Sem-Sandberg argues the mythorealist poetics is a formal contribution; Carlberg, Palm, Mattson and Sward cannot judge the Chinese prose directly and treat coverage as partial.

Whether Yoko Tawada's shorter, episodic and bilingual forms sustain depth at the scale of a whole authorship. Sward and Olsson see a real formal achievement but share the doubt; Mattson and Carlberg did not rank her and say their knowledge is thinner.

Whether Adonis's achievement in the prosody and inherited forms of Arabic poetry can be judged adequately through translation (Palm and Sem-Sandberg raise this; Carlberg stresses the linguistic significance), and how essays should be weighed against poetry.
Whether Alexis Wright's compact oeuvre, centered on two large novels, allows a judgment of sustained quality (Palm raises this herself; Olsson and Carlberg ranked Wright seventh).
attribution_disputes: No attribution dispute is explicit in the files: every entry credits one writer, and all six files describe the B050 citation as a single-author citation raising no attribution problem.

Proposals differ in laureate across the second tier (B009, B018, B001, B013, B039, B024), but none is combined with B050 in a multiwriter configuration; these differences concern who, not how the citation is scoped.

Citation scope is the one live scoping question. For B009 the files agree the citation must be limited to the written poems, excluding landscape-scale and non-textual work. For B050, the six submitted wordings differ slightly in naming Romanian, prose and poetry together, and metaphysical or historical reach, but not in laureate.
maturity_disputes: For B050, whether the poetry, essays and early prose are known well enough to support a whole-oeuvre claim. Carlberg, Palm, Sem-Sandberg and Sward say the case is partly inferred from the major novels, and Olsson says his coverage of the poetry and early work is thinner.
Whether the later Cărtărescu volumes show development or only enlargement (see merit disputes). This bears directly on the sustained-quality criterion.

For B009, whether a single sequential poetic project over decades shows sustained depth or recurring technique (Sem-Sandberg's question), and whether its force depends on its historical occasion (Mattson and Palm).
For B001 and B039, whether a more compact body of work has the cumulative weight for the prize. Mattson acknowledges this for NDiaye; Palm acknowledges it for Wright.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: All six round-1 files report no apparent conflict from the supplied profiles. No recusal is requested or proposed, and no file claims to have verified this beyond the profiles.

Chair disclosure: my opening ranking placed Zurita (B009) first and Cărtărescu (B050) second, and my round-1 file moves B050 to first with B009 as the first alternative. The shift is disclosed here and is recorded in my file as a weighing of merit arguments.

Chair context: my scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, nihilism and exile literature is context only, not evidence of a connection to any shortlisted writer, and the same applies to the other members' declared fields of practice.
Sem-Sandberg discloses his Central European and Prague/Vienna ties as context only and says he does not treat regional familiarity as merit.
Carlberg is a co-opted member whose actual committee voting status is undocumented, so her simulated vote is a modeling assumption (stated in her own file).
The committee recommendation modeled here is not the decision of the full Swedish Academy, which is not simulated.
questions_for_round2: Which specific Cărtărescu works (Orbitor/Blinding, Solenoid, the poetry, the essays) will each member rely on, and what concrete evidence from the later volumes shows whether they deepen the project or repeat its motifs?

Can any member who reads Romanian, or the anonymous regional expert reports where available, say how much of the syntactic and rhythmic design of Cărtărescu's prose survives in the translations the committee actually uses?

If B009 is raised in the final discussion, can the citation be worded strictly around the written sequences (Purgatory, Anteparadise), and do those sequences carry the case on their own in Spanish, separate from the landscape interventions and historical occasion?

Among the second-tier alternatives (B009, B018, B001, B013, B024, B039), which one or two does each member wish to argue as a serious alternative to B050, and on which specific works and merit criteria rather than on rank?
Can Mattson specify which NDiaye works carry the main claim across decades, and can Sward and Olsson say what evidence would show that Tawada's shorter forms sustain depth across Japanese and German?

Is there reliable evidence on the Chinese and Arabic originals that would let the committee weigh Yan Lianke's corpus for uneven quality and Adonis's prosodic renewal, or should those cases be reserved for later years?
Does any member see a reason, on merit or citation grounds, to hold back from B050 or to prefer no award (P000) this year, and is any such reservation explicit enough to record?
summary.chair_observation: In round 1 all six files explicitly prefer B050 as a single-writer configuration, with a shared merit rationale and a shared reservation about translation and late-volume repetition. The files hold a wider spread on second-tier alternatives and on how much evidence is available for poetry candidates. Every assessment rests on public knowledge and not on fresh reading, so the shared position is only as strong as the unresolved questions about translation, corpus coverage and sustained quality in the late work. This summary records positions and open questions for round 2 and does not rule on merit or on any vote outcome.
